title: Rav Ada son of Rav Azza
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He said in Rav Assi’s name: Kiddushin 81b. Hyman considers it very likely that he came with all the travelers [from the Land of Israel] in Abaye’s time, and he is the one mentioned in Temurah 21a: “Rava son of Rav Azza said: They asked in the West — Abaye said to him.” He conjectures that it was written רב״א, an abbreviation for Rav Ada. Yuchasin’s reading there was Rav Acha son of Rav Azza; and where it cites “Rav Acha son of Rav Azza said: Rav Abaye,” he proposes reading “Abaye said to him.”

notes.text: The entry’s subject reports Rav Assi; the opening does not merely quote Rav Assi as an unrelated speaker. Saved Davidson Kiddushin 81b has Ada bar Rav Azza/Avva, and Temurah 21a has Rava bar Rav Azza and an alternative Acha reading. Hyman’s travelers inference, abbreviation reconstruction and Abaye correction remain qualified; the father-name variant is not erased.
